LOAD A CHARACTER

DEMO CHARACTERS

Demo humans: "Human Models Set – Male/Female (Rigged)" by lzyassoul on Sketchfab, CC BY. Credit them if you use these in a game.

Works best with one humanoid character standing in a T-pose or A-pose, arms away from the body, legs slightly apart. GLB, FBX, OBJ and STL (from Onshape, Tinkercad, Sketchfab, etc).

ORIENTATION

The character should stand upright and face you (front of the view).

PLACE THE MARKERS

Drag each dot onto the character's chin, wrists, elbows, knees and groin. The blue lines preview the skeleton.

"L" means the character's own left, which is on your right when it faces you.

RIG

FIX WEIGHTS (OPTIONAL)

If part of the mesh stretches the wrong way, paint how much each bone moves it.

0%100%

While painting, right-drag to orbit, scroll to zoom.

Build the rig first (step 2).

ANIMATIONS

Click to preview. Ticked ones are included in the export.

1.00×

TEST DRIVE

WASD / arrows move · Shift run · Space jump · F punch · Esc stop

MAKE YOUR OWN ANIMATION

Pose a bone, add a key, pose again, add another key… then save.

0 keys

COLOURS & TEXTURES

Change each material's colour, shine and metal, or put an image texture on it.

EXPORT FOR YOUR GAME

Exports a .glb with the mesh, skeleton, materials and every ticked animation. It loads in Three.js, Godot, Unity (with glTFast), Unreal, Blender and more.

TIPS

Bones use Mixamo-style names (mixamorigHips, mixamorigLeftArm…), so code written for Mixamo characters usually works.

In Three.js: load with GLTFLoader, make an AnimationMixer on the scene, and play gltf.animations by name (Idle, Walk, Run, Jump, Wave, Punch, Death).

Everything stays on this computer. Nothing is uploaded.
